**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Charge the mail budget only for a successfully claimed job**

When two mail workers select the same pending job, both can consume daily quota here before either claims it. Only one subsequently sends the message; the other skips it at the pending-state recheck without releasing its quota reservation. Running the dispatch function with two synchronized workers and a daily limit of two reproduced one submitted email, an exhausted budget, and a second eligible email left pending. This can delay unrelated reminders until the 24-hour budget resets. Make quota reservation atomic with claiming the job, or release reservations when the subsequent validation skips submission, while retaining the live-clock recheck.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind the clock baseline to the cached list's revision**

If a user leaves a cached task list, receives a new task while viewing the dashboard, and then returns to the same list filters, the dashboard has already advanced the shared workspace projection's baseline while the paged collection still contains its old records. Subsequent clock refreshes therefore report `baseline_known: true` and `stable_changed: false`; the loaded-row comparison also passes because the existing tasks are unchanged. For ordinary filters such as `pending` or `all`, this permanently skips reloading the list, hiding the new task and retaining the old total until another mutation or explicit refresh. This reproduces using the actual projection, paged-list, and clock controllers across route changes. Compare against a revision associated with the paged collection, or invalidate that collection when an off-route stable update occurs, rather than treating the projection cache's baseline as the list's baseline.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Charge the mail budget only for a successfully claimed job**

When two mail workers select the same pending job, both can consume daily quota here before either claims it. Only one subsequently sends the message; the other skips it at the pending-state recheck without releasing its quota reservation. Running the dispatch function with two synchronized workers and a daily limit of two reproduced one submitted email, an exhausted budget, and a second eligible email left pending. This can delay unrelated reminders until the 24-hour budget resets. Make quota reservation atomic with claiming the job, or release reservations when the subsequent validation skips submission, while retaining the live-clock recheck.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind the clock baseline to the cached list's revision**

If a user leaves a cached task list, receives a new task while viewing the dashboard, and then returns to the same list filters, the dashboard has already advanced the shared workspace projection's baseline while the paged collection still contains its old records. Subsequent clock refreshes therefore report `baseline_known: true` and `stable_changed: false`; the loaded-row comparison also passes because the existing tasks are unchanged. For ordinary filters such as `pending` or `all`, this permanently skips reloading the list, hiding the new task and retaining the old total until another mutation or explicit refresh. This reproduces using the actual projection, paged-list, and clock controllers across route changes. Compare against a revision associated with the paged collection, or invalidate that collection when an off-route stable update occurs, rather than treating the projection cache's baseline as the list's baseline.

A controller reproduction retains version 1 after a committed version-2 mutation and makes no post-mutation page request. Honor `force` here, or otherwise ensure a mutation-triggered refresh cannot reuse a request started before that mutation.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind the clock baseline to the cached list's revision**

If a user leaves a cached task list, receives a new task while viewing the dashboard, and then returns to the same list filters, the dashboard has already advanced the shared workspace projection's baseline while the paged collection still contains its old records. Subsequent clock refreshes therefore report `baseline_known: true` and `stable_changed: false`; the loaded-row comparison also passes because the existing tasks are unchanged. For ordinary filters such as `pending` or `all`, this permanently skips reloading the list, hiding the new task and retaining the old total until another mutation or explicit refresh. This reproduces using the actual projection, paged-list, and clock controllers across route changes. Compare against a revision associated with the paged collection, or invalidate that collection when an off-route stable update occurs, rather than treating the projection cache's baseline as the list's baseline.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Honor forced range refreshes after a committed mutation**

If a board move or undo completes while a background range refresh is still pending, `loadTaskList(true, {preserveRange:true})` reaches this branch and reuses the pre-mutation request: neither the shared projection revision nor the invalidation counter necessarily advances before the subsequent sync probe. That request's `canApply` closure is now invalid because the successful mutation incremented `workspaceMutation`, so both callers resolve to `null` without fetching the saved board state. This leaves the card in its old position until another sync succeeds, despite reporting that the move was saved. A controller reproduction retains version 1 after a committed version-2 mutation and makes no post-mutation page request. Honor `force` here, or otherwise ensure a mutation-triggered refresh cannot reuse a request started before that mutation.
